institution_name: University of the West Indies - Cave Hill

coverage.notes: Catalogue scope: Cave Hill lists more than 200 multidisciplinary undergraduate degrees within a catalogue exceeding 350 programmes across all levels, delivered generally in English. Four deliberately selective first-year flagships were researched from the campus undergraduate catalogue, December 2025 quick guide and faculty pages; this is not an exhaustive list. The programme search offers an Undergraduate filter and A-Z/faculty browsing, but its A-Z data are client-loaded. Published entry documentation concerns academic year 2026/27 (main intake August 2026), and the currently linked fee booklet concerns 2025/26. August 2027 course continuation, qualification equivalences, dates and fees remain to be reconfirmed; postgraduate, exchange-only and diploma-only pathways are excluded.

institution.summary: English-taught Barbados campus of the University of the West Indies, with seven faculties and a broad undergraduate programme catalogue.

programmes.name: Computer Science
programmes.campus: Cave Hill Campus, St. Michael, Barbados
programmes.about: A Bachelor of Science major combining the practical development of computing solutions with the mathematical and theoretical foundations of computer science.
programmes.overview: The Computer Science major examines how computation and information work while developing the ability to turn problems into practical computing solutions. First-year study includes programming-oriented Computing I and II, mathematics for computer science, UNIX and an introduction to entrepreneurship. Both coursework and final examinations contribute to assessment in computing courses. Students can explore related combinations with other science disciplines or selected social sciences, subject to the applicable degree structure.

programmes.name: Environmental Science
programmes.campus: Cave Hill Campus, St. Michael, Barbados
programmes.about: A Bachelor of Science major studying environmental systems, climate, oceans and landforms with applications to Caribbean and global environmental challenges.
programmes.overview: This major begins with Earth and environmental systems, oceans and climate, and landform dynamics, then moves into oceanography, Earth life cycles and climate science. Electives cover areas such as biodiversity, sustainable energy, natural hazards, pollution assessment and environmental law. The department identifies field trips and opportunities to use local research settings, with some courses involving work on land or at sea. The degree develops scientific understanding relevant to environmental assessment, conservation and resource management.

programmes.name: BFA Film (Special)
programmes.campus: Cave Hill Campus, St. Michael, Barbados
programmes.about: A Bachelor of Fine Arts film specialisation blending cinema analysis, storytelling, digital media production and practical moving-image work.
programmes.overview: Film study combines analysis of cinema as an art form with hands-on digital image, sound and moving-picture production. Introductory work addresses film form, narrative and digital media workflows; later film courses consider Caribbean cinema, cinematic history, theory and motion graphics. Practical assignments develop skills in recording, editing and communicating through screen media. Candidates also demonstrate creative interests through a submitted film, selected clips or a photographic portfolio during the admissions process.

programmes.name: LL.B. Degree (Bachelor of Laws)
programmes.campus: Cave Hill Campus, St. Michael, Barbados
programmes.about: A three-year Bachelor of Laws providing a foundation in legal reasoning, written argument and substantive areas of Caribbean and international law.
programmes.overview: The LL.B. develops knowledge of legal rules alongside the skills needed to identify issues, assess arguments and prepare clear written legal opinions. Subject areas identified by the faculty include criminal law, real property law and international law, with particular attention to legal method. Students can use a dedicated law library and online Caribbean and international legal resources. The faculty also connects these skills to work in justice administration, public affairs and other settings where legal knowledge is valuable.
